findings.title: restraint field includes limit and intellect
findings.claim: The prohibition can carry a bounded pressure of endpoint and disciplined judgment while remaining a command to forbid.
findings.mechanism: Naha is the carrier; an al-munkar supplies an explicit boundary away from wrong, and the recognized-good/wrong contrast supplies a separate cue for reasoned discernment. These contacts make restraint feel like a stop-line rather than a bare negative.
findings.reader_payoff: The command becomes legible as both a boundary against wrongdoing and an act of judgment.
findings.containment: Naha still commands forbidding; boundary and judgment color the prohibition without replacing that local sense.

epistemic.reason: The trusted word analysis marks endpoint and intellect as secondary pressure; both have independent focus triggers in the separation complement and the recognized/rejected pair.

findings.title: forbid-wrong mirrors enjoin-right
findings.claim: Enjoining good and forbidding wrong mirror each other as constructive and protective public duties.
findings.mechanism: The two coordinate imperatives take opposite ethical complements, bi-l-ma'ruf and an al-munkar, so the positive act of promoting good is paired with a boundary against wrong.
findings.reader_payoff: Public responsibility includes both what to encourage and what to resist.
findings.containment: The mirror preserves two separate commands and does not reduce either to the other.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows from trusted, accepted focus alignment and directly supplied local syntax or morphology.

findings.containment: The prepositions retain their separate local grammar and do not turn the duties into a single act.
